title: Design System: Nokia AirScale / Flexi Zone XML Explorer

title.purpose: File name, explanation subject, dialog titles, empty-workspace heading. The only role that steps up in size.

body.purpose: Prose: explanation text, dialog copy, empty states, toasts. 1.55 line height for prose, 1.4 in chrome.

label.purpose: Controls, pane titles, section headers, metadata, counts, badges, tags. 600 for titles, headers and filled-button labels.

data.purpose: Everything from the file: tree labels, values, raw XML, distNames, the Trace address. Managed objects at 600 in full ink.

chip.purpose: Sidebar per-file metadata chips only (release, band, ARFCN), one step down so they stay on one line. Not a general role.

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Context menu, release filter, History popover, toasts: things that float and dismiss.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs only, over the Modal Scrim.

shadows.name: selection-ring
shadows.purpose: Selected tree row, raw row, file and folder; composes over row tints without shifting layout.

shadows.name: hover-veil
shadows.purpose: Row hover in tree and raw panes; overlays official/red/signal tints instead of replacing them.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus everywhere (offset -2px on rows and list items). Text fields mark focus with a yellow border instead.

motion.name: ease-route
motion.purpose: The one easing curve: Trace draw-in and toast entry.

motion.name: trace-in
motion.value: 200ms ease-route, transform scaleY(0 to 1) from the top, +35ms delay per depth
motion.purpose: The lit Trace route pours from root to the selected row, level by level. Trace's one authored motion.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.value: 180ms ease-route, opacity 0 to 1 and translateY(6px to 0)

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): animation none; scroll sync jumps
motion.purpose: Both animations switch off; pane scroll sync jumps instead of gliding.

motion.name: state-changes
motion.purpose: Hover, selection and toggles change without transitions.

breakpoints.name: file-header-compact
breakpoints.purpose: File header hides button labels and the unverified count.

breakpoints.name: toolbar-compact
breakpoints.purpose: Tree toolbar hides expand/collapse labels; icons keep accessible names.

breakpoints.name: file-header-min
breakpoints.purpose: File header hides object/parameter counts and the read-only note.

breakpoints.name: raw-toolbar-wrap
breakpoints.purpose: Raw XML toolbar wraps instead of pushing controls off-screen.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: One scrolling column: files, workspace (88vh), explanation; value column capped at 46vw.

narrative.overview:
The explorer takes its visual language from the TIA-598 fiber colour code. A cable has a black jacket, off-white lettering printed along it, and a fixed sequence of hues that tells a splicer which fibre sits where. Here the fibre is a managed object and its position is its distName. Ground and text stay neutral. Colour does three jobs: showing depth (the fiber-code sequence drawn as thin guides), showing state (three hues that each mean one thing) and reading data (values and raw XML syntax in their own bright colours, as in a code editor). Selecting a row lights its lineage as a route of code hues from the root down to that row, and the same route appears as a banded address in the file header. That move, Trace, is the system's signature.

The density suits an engineer at work. Tree, raw XML and explanation share one optical text size. Rows are 22px tall and spacing steps by 4px. Each pane is its own rounded panel floating on a darker page, with an 8px gutter between panels that doubles as the resize handle. Rank comes from weight (400 or 600) and four ink strengths rather than from size. Values line up at a fixed column like a departures board, so a run of parameters can be scanned top to bottom. Motion is nearly absent: the Trace route draws in once, a toast rises into place, and nothing else animates.

The palette is one of three dark themes, picked in the app bar and remembered per browser: **Night** (the default, indigo panels with neon-pastel accents), **Slate** (a lifted cool slate with vivid accents) and **GitHub** (close to the original blue-black look, punchier). Every theme fills the same roles, so no hue does two jobs in any of them. The tool is dark only, and it carries no Nokia logo, Nokia brand colour or anything that could read as an official Nokia product.
keyCharacteristics: Three dark themes (Night, Slate, GitHub) on one token vocabulary: a page ground, four panel ground steps and four ink strengths each.
Fiber-code hues appear only as 1–2px depth guides, 8px address swatches and the wordmark's Trace glyph.
Three state hues with one meaning each: yellow for focus, selection and action; aqua for Official provenance; red for gaps and errors.
Trace: the selected row's lineage drawn as a lit route and mirrored as a banded distName address.
One optical size (13px mono data, 14px condensed UI), ranked by weight and ink.
Rounded, hairline-edged panels on a darker page; shadows only on things that float.

rules.name: The Same Roles Rule
rules.body: A theme changes colours, never meanings. Every theme defines the same base tokens, and all tints, rings and dims are derived from them. A new theme is a new block of base colours, nothing else.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each state hue has exactly one job. The signal is never a warning, the official hue is never a link or a selection, and red is never decoration. There is no amber or caution state: a fact the user should weigh is a neutral note on Raised Sheath in full ink.

rules.name: The Quieter-Than-Focus Rule
rules.body: The official hue is a tint and a badge, never a stripe or a fill in the tree. Selection always wins: a selected row shows the soft signal tint and the signal ring, whatever tint it sits on.

rules.name: The One Optical Size Rule
rules.body: 14px UI text and 13px mono data share an x-height, and that pair is the system's single size. Rank within it comes from weight (400 or 600) and ink strength. Only titles step up and only the sidebar chips step down. Add no new sizes.

rules.name: The As-Written Rule
rules.body: Ligatures and contextual alternates are off everywhere (`font-variant-ligatures: none`), so `>-13` or `!=` never fuse in the mono. Numerals are tabular everywhere (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`), so counts, sizes and ARFCNs line up digit for digit.

rules.name: The Syntax Colour Rule
rules.body: Raw XML is highlighted like a code editor: punctuation in `syn-punct`, tag names in `syn-tag`, attribute names in `syn-attr`, attribute values in `syn-val` and text content in `syn-text`. Search matches are found on the whole line and split back along token edges, so a query like `name="pMax"` marks across tokens.

rules.name: The Departures Board Rule
rules.body: Tree values align in one column. Its width is measured per file from the widest label (with its indent and row furniture), clamped to 240–560px, and each row's label cell is that width minus its own indent, never under 8rem. Below 900px the column is capped at 46vw and long labels ellipsize.

rules.name: The Shed-Before-Wrap Rule
rules.body: The file header and toolbars respond to their own width through container queries, because the side panes resize independently of the window. They shed secondary text first: button labels at 880px (header) and 860px (toolbar), then the counts and the read-only note at 640px. Wrapping is the last resort; the raw toolbar wraps only below 560px. The file name and the Edit and Download actions are never dropped.

rules.name: The Flat Panes Rule
rules.body: Panels, rows and controls never cast shadows. Only something that floats above the workspace and can be dismissed gets one, and it uses Pop or Modal, nothing in between.

rules.name: The Ruled Rows Rule
rules.body: Collections are rows separated by 1px hairlines, never a card per item. Rounded panels are for the regions of the shell, not for the items inside them. This covers the file list, Site Management's files, the Required Fields table, History and the explanation's key/value pairs. Never put a card inside a modal's own card.

rules.name: The Focus Outranks Rule
rules.body: The selected or active row is the strongest state on screen. Soft yellow and the yellow ring override the Official tint, the required-missing tint and the hover veil.

rules.name: The Change Stays Lit Rule
rules.body: A value edited in this session keeps a 6px yellow dot before it, in both the tree and the raw pane, until the file is closed. Nothing changes silently.

rules.name: The One Fill Rule
rules.body: Solid yellow belongs to the single action that moves the job forward. Toggles, selections and hovers use the soft fill, never the solid one.

dos: Do add or change a theme only as a block of base colours in styles.css (`:root[data-theme="…"]`); let every tint, ring and dim derive from them.
Do draw depth only with the fiber-code hues in order, blue at the root: the `-dim` hue for resting guides, the full hue for the lit route and address swatches, and dashes for the second cycle.
Do mark any new "selected" state with `signal-soft` and the 1px `signal-line` ring, and keep the solid yellow fill for the one forward action.
Do show Official provenance as an aqua row tint or pill badge, and let selection override it.
Do set file data in the mono and the UI's own words in Barlow Semi Condensed at the one optical size, ranking with 400/600 and ink strength.
Do align values to the measured value column in any new tree-like list.
Do separate panes and list items with 1px hairlines and save shadows for things that float.
Do adapt headers and toolbars with container queries, shedding labels before anything wraps.
Do draw new icons on the 16px grid with a 1.5px round stroke in `currentColor`.
Do switch off every animation under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't let one accent colour do every job; each theme keeps signal, official and danger distinct.
Don't put red, yellow, aqua or black into the depth sequence, or use a depth hue for anything but a guide line or a Trace swatch.
Don't introduce an amber or caution hue; a fact to weigh is a neutral note.
Don't make Official a stripe, a fill, or louder than selection.
Don't add type sizes beyond the five roles, or turn ligatures back on.
Don't hard-code a colour in a component; reference a role token so every theme works.
Don't render lists as cards, and never nest a card inside a modal.
Don't add a light theme; the tool is dark only.
Don't use Nokia logos, Nokia brand colours or anything that could read as an official Nokia product.
Don't use emoji, unicode glyphs or an icon font as icons.
Don't extend the Trace route below the selected row, or add hover transitions and decorative motion; Trace's draw-in and the toast's entry are the only animations.
